title: Micchami Dukkadam sirf sorry nahi — teeno fold ka formula kya hai
hooks: Micchami Dukkadam sirf sorry nahi hai
Tino fold kholte hain Paryushan ka asli raaz
Ek shloka mein chhupa hai poora karma reset
hook_why: Opens with a direct contrarian statement that challenges the common misconception in the first 4 words. No setup, no greeting — immediate curiosity spike.
metaphor: Three lotus petals opening one by one on a white marble step, each glowing with warm golden light — each petal represents one fold of the forgiveness formula, blooming in sequence.
mechanism: Speaker utters first fold: Khamemi Savve Jiva — I forgive all living beings
Speaker utters second fold: Savve Jiva Khamantu Me — May all living beings forgive me
Speaker utters third fold: Mitti Me Savva Bhuyesu Veram Majjham Na Kenai — Friendship with all, enmity with none
Recited during Samvatsari Pratikramana as prescribed in Agam (Airyapathiki Sutra, Yoga sastra verse 3.124)
Extends beyond humans to every jiva — ants, plants, unseen beings — resetting karmic ledger for the new year

caption:
Micchami Dukkadam sirf 'sorry' nahi — yeh teeno fold ka ek purana formula hai jo Agam mein likha hai. Pehle main sabko maaf karta hoon, phir sabse maaf maangta hoon, aur aakhir mein dosti sabse, dushmani kisi se nahi. Ye sirf insanon tak nahi, cheenti-patte tak pahuncha hai. Paryushan ke aakhri din Samvatsari (Digambar mein Kshamavani) yehi teen baar doharaya jata hai. Karma reset. Naya saal shuru.

Aap kaunsi fold sabse mushkil maante hain?

claims.claim: Micchami Dukkadam is a Prakrit phrase meaning 'may my bad deeds be fruitless' used in Jain Pratikramana ritual
claims.basis: Wikipedia: Michchhāmi Dukkaḍaṃ is an ancient Indian Prakrit language phrase found in historic Jain texts, used in Pratikramana ritual every nine days and on Samvatsari

claims.claim: The threefold forgiveness formula consists of: Khamemi Savve Jiva (I forgive all living beings), Savve Jiva Khamantu Me (May all living beings forgive me), Mitti Me Savva Bhuyesu Veram Majjham Na Kenai (Friendship with all, enmity with none)
claims.basis: thejainreligion.in: The forgiveness prayer includes these three lines in Prakrit with Hindi translation

claims.claim: The formula is recited during Samvatsari Pratikramana on the last day of Paryushan (Svetambara) and Kshamavani (Digambara)
claims.basis: Wikipedia: Used on the last day of Paryushana called Samvatsari in Svetambara tradition, and Kshamavani in Digambara tradition

claims.claim: The phrase appears in the Airyapathiki Sutra and Yoga sastra (Hemachandra's Yogasastra verse 3.124)
claims.basis: Wikipedia: Found in Airyapathiki Sutra, verses 3.124 and 3.130 of the Yoga sastra; Hemachandra gave symbolic etymological basis in Yogasastra verse 3.124

claims.claim: The forgiveness extends to all living beings (jiva) including unseen beings like ants, plants, microorganisms
claims.basis: pandasbox.in: 'All living beings. Not just Mum. Not just Dad. Not just the friend you fought with yesterday. Everyone.' Includes ants, flowers, unseen beings hurt unknowingly
